title: A rise in the price level: money demand, the nominal interest rate and bond prices
scenario: The price level in the invented country of Wren rises, and its central bank keeps the money supply unchanged.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Draw a correctly labeled graph of the money market and show the effect of the rise in the price level on the nominal interest rate.

rubric.point: A correctly labeled money market: nominal interest rate on the vertical axis, quantity of money on the horizontal axis, downward-sloping MD and vertical MS

accept: MD1 to MD2 to the right

rubric.point: A higher nominal interest rate shown on the vertical axis (i2 above i1)
accept: i rises from i1 to i2

parts.sample: Vertical axis: nominal interest rate (i). Horizontal axis: quantity of money. The vertical MS crosses MD1 at i1. The higher price level shifts money demand right to MD2, which crosses MS at i2, above i1; the quantity of money is unchanged.

key.because: a rise in the price level

slips.MS: The central bank keeps the money supply unchanged. A higher price level raises how much money people need: money demand shifts.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Explain why money demand changes when the price level rises.

rubric.point: Explains that at higher prices people need more money for the same purchases (transaction demand rises)
accept: nominal GDP rises so more money is needed for transactions

parts.sample: With a higher price level, each purchase costs more, so households and firms need to hold more money to make the same transactions. The transaction demand for money rises at every interest rate.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Based on your answer to part A, explain what happens to the prices of existing bonds in Wren.

rubric.point: States that bond prices fall, because bond prices move opposite to interest rates (people sell bonds to get money)
accept: bond prices decrease because the interest rate rose

parts.sample: Bond prices fall. To hold more money, people sell bonds, which pushes bond prices down; that is why the interest rate rises, since bond prices and interest rates move in opposite directions.
